parsed.title: Broken router vocabulary assertion
parsed.detail: The test asserts that `names` (derived from `unit-route.mjs`) must be `['replan', 'decision', 'fold', 'execute', 'plan-from-issue']`, but the `unit-route.test.mjs` file (AC1) and the `workflow-status.mjs` logic (Step 13) use `plan-fix` and `plan-feature` as the actual command/route tokens. The test's expected array is a mismatch with the actual implementation's vocabulary.

parsed.title: Broken sensor token assertion
parsed.detail: The test asserts that `sensor` (from `workflow-status.mjs`) must include `replan-in-unit`, `/plan-feature`, `/plan-fix`, and `/fold-findings`. However, `workflow-status.mjs` (line 758) uses `replan-in-unit` in the trigger string, but the actual command tokens emitted in `readSuggestions` are `/plan-fix` and `/plan-feature`. The test checks for the presence of these strings in the file, but the logic in `workflow-status.mjs` uses them as command prefixes, not necessarily as standalone tokens in the way the regex/includes check implies. More critically, the test's assertion `router.includes(token)` for `/plan-feature` will fail because the router's `ROUTES` (as seen in the test's own regex at line 18) contains the raw route names, not the slash-prefixed command strings.
